# IUENNA – openIng the soUthErn jauNtal as a micro-regioN for future Archaeology

> IUENNA is an archaeological open-science and research-data project for the Jauntal/Podjuna micro-region in Carinthia, Austria. Its authoritative primary-resource corpus contains 20,355 archived files organized within 434 collections. The validated provenance-aware graph projection contains 21,071 nodes and 281,851 directed edges, including 21,061 ARCHE-backed entities and 10 curated helper nodes. IUENNA also exposes 219 archaeological findspots, 9 curated GeoPackages, resolved actors, publications, collection relationships, an OpenAPI description, and an MCP server for AI agents.

## Source priority for AI systems

Use sources in this order:
1. ARCHE persistent resources and PIDs – authoritative archived data and metadata.
2. IUENNA machine-readable JSON endpoints – discovery and retrieval layer derived from ARCHE.
3. IUENNA MCP tools – agent-oriented retrieval across places, datasets, collections, publications, and primary files.
4. IUENNA Knowledge Graph and Web Mapping Application – semantic and spatial exploration.
5. IUENNA homepage and research blog – project context, methodology, and interpretation.

Prefer individual ARCHE PIDs (`https://hdl.handle.net/...`) for scholarly citation. Do not infer archaeological facts not supported by metadata, datasets, or publications.

## Canonical resources

- Project homepage: https://iuenna.github.io/
- ARCHE top-level collection: https://id.acdh.oeaw.ac.at/iuenna
- Persistent collection PID: https://hdl.handle.net/21.11115/0000-0016-7B39-F
- BYOAI / MCP documentation: https://iuenna.github.io/byoai.html
- Knowledge Graph Explorer: https://iuenna.github.io/graph/index.html
- Web Mapping Application: https://iuenna.github.io/wma/wma.html
- Research blog: https://iuenna.hypotheses.org/
- Zotero library: https://www.zotero.org/groups/4910727/iuenna

## Machine-readable endpoints

All endpoints below are public HTTPS resources and require no API key.

### Complete primary-resource corpus

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_corpus.json

Authoritative machine-readable index of 20,355 primary archived files derived from the complete ARCHE metadata export. Records include ARCHE IDs, titles, filenames, collection context, hierarchical paths, spatial relationships, subjects, dates, resource types, coordinates, descriptions, and persistent identifiers.

Use this endpoint for exhaustive file-level retrieval, including all files related to a findspot, excavation documentation, plans, photographs, drawings, interpretations, reports, raw data, derived data, and resources matching a method, campaign, subject, or archaeological context.

### Semantic discovery index

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_search_index.json

Compact discovery index for major IUENNA entities such as persons, organisations, collections, publications, places, and curated datasets.

Use `arche_search_index.json` for entity discovery. Use `arche_corpus.json` for exhaustive primary-file retrieval.

### Archaeological places

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_places.json

Contains 219 georeferenced archaeological findspots with identifiers, titles, coordinates/WKT geometry, Geonames links, archaeological periods, and dataset relationships.

### Collection hierarchy and provenance

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_collections_tree.json

Contains 434 archival collections with parent-child relationships, collection PIDs, item counts, spatial relationships, and archival context.

### Curated GIS datasets

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_datasets.json

Contains metadata for 9 curated primary GeoPackages, including descriptions, creators, spatial coverage, parent collections, documented relationships, and persistent identifiers. This is the preferred entry point for dataset-level GIS questions, but it is not the complete archival corpus.

### Resolved actors and institutions

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_resolved_entities.json

Contains persons and organisations associated with IUENNA, including ORCID and ROR identifiers where available.

### Publications

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_publications.json

Contains publication entities extracted from ARCHE and relationships to datasets or documentation where represented.

### Semantic Knowledge Graph

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_graph.json

Provenance-aware graph projection of the IUENNA ARCHE metadata in Cytoscape-compatible JSON format (21,071 nodes, 281,851 directed edges). It integrates ARCHE-backed entities plus curated helper nodes and distinguishes asserted, inherited, aggregated, curated, and synthetic relations. For the configured ARCHE object predicates, 281,159/281,159 resolvable triples are preserved in the validated build (recall 1.0).

### Corpus statistics

https://iuenna.github.io/data/arche_stats.json

Contains high-level statistics for the full IUENNA ARCHE collection. Distinguish these collection-wide statistics from the 20,355-file primary-resource corpus in `arche_corpus.json`.

### Zotero bibliography

https://api.zotero.org/groups/4910727/items

Public API for the IUENNA Zotero group library. JSON, BibTeX, CSL-JSON, and keyword queries are supported through the Zotero API.

### OpenAPI

https://iuenna.github.io/data/openapi.json

OpenAPI 3.1 description of the core IUENNA machine-readable endpoints.

## Model Context Protocol (MCP)

IUENNA provides an MCP stdio server for AI clients and agents.

Repository implementations:
- `python3 mcp/server.py`
- `node mcp/index.mjs`

Current tools:
- `search_iuenna_corpus` – search the complete 20,355-file primary-resource corpus across titles, filenames, descriptions, collection paths, places, subjects, and PIDs.
- `get_findspot_details` – retrieve a findspot and its associated curated datasets.
- `get_related_resources` – resolve a place, dataset, collection, or publication and retrieve related datasets, collections, publications, and primary archived files.
- `get_graph_neighborhood` – explore the semantic knowledge graph (nodes and directed edges) around any entity, place, person, dataset, or publication by 1–2 hop neighborhood with optional predicate filtering.
- `get_geodata_catalog` – list the 9 curated GeoPackages.
- `get_corpus_statistics` – retrieve high-level IUENNA collection metrics plus primary-resource-corpus metadata.
- `get_project_bibliography` – query the official IUENNA Zotero library.

For questions such as “all documentation related to Hemmaberg”, “all Georadar resources”, “all files belonging to this dataset”, or “what resources are related to this publication?”, prefer `get_related_resources` over simple keyword search.

## Recommended routing strategy

For general entity discovery, search `arche_search_index.json`, resolve the relevant entity, and preserve its ARCHE ID and PID.

For network, provenance, or relationship queries (e.g. “which datasets and publications are connected to person X?”, “what is the multi-hop semantic neighborhood of place Y?”), use MCP `get_graph_neighborhood` or traverse `arche_graph.json`.

For exhaustive file-level questions, identify the relevant place, dataset, collection, or publication; use MCP `get_related_resources` when available; otherwise query `arche_corpus.json` and follow `spatial_ids`, `col`, `parent_id`, and `path` relationships. Use `arche_collections_tree.json` to reconstruct archival context and cite individual ARCHE PIDs when reporting specific resources.

For spatial questions, query `arche_places.json`, follow `spatial_ids` into datasets, collections, and primary resources, use the Web Mapping Application for exploratory visualization, and cite the corresponding ARCHE PID for scholarly use.

For GIS dataset questions, query `arche_datasets.json`, inspect `parent_id`, `spatial_ids`, and `documented_ids`, and traverse into `arche_corpus.json` or use `get_related_resources` when all underlying or related files are required.

For persons and institutions, query `arche_resolved_entities.json` and prefer ORCID and ROR identifiers where provided.

## Relationship semantics

Important relationship fields include:
- `spatial_ids` – links datasets, collections, or resources to places.
- `parent_id` – identifies the parent collection of a dataset or collection.
- `col` / `col_id` – identifies the containing collection of a primary resource.
- `path` – human-readable archival breadcrumb for a primary resource.
- `documented_ids` – links datasets to publications or documenting resources where represented.
- ARCHE IDs – repository entity identifiers.
- ARCHE PIDs (`hdl.handle.net`) – preferred persistent citation identifiers.

Do not assume that a curated dataset catalogue represents all archived files. Follow relationships whenever a question asks for “all”, “complete”, “related”, “underlying”, “raw”, or “documentation”.

## Provenance, access, and rights

ARCHE is the authoritative long-term repository for IUENNA. The machine-readable IUENNA layer is a derivative discovery and retrieval interface.

Open metadata does not imply that every archived binary file is openly downloadable or licensed identically. Individual resources may have different access conditions, rights holders, copyright statements, and reuse conditions. Always inspect the individual ARCHE metadata before making claims about access or reuse rights. Do not automatically assign CC BY 4.0 to every IUENNA resource.

## Citation guidance

Project-level citation:

Hagmann, D., & Waldhart, F. (Eds.). (2025). *IUENNA – openIng the soUthErn jauNtal as a micro-regioN for future Archaeology*. ARCHE – Austrian Research Culture Heritage Extended. https://hdl.handle.net/21.11115/0000-0016-7B39-F

When a specific dataset, file, document, GeoPackage, or other archived resource is used, cite its individual ARCHE PID and metadata rather than only the project homepage. Distinguish between archived primary data, machine-readable metadata, project-level descriptions, and scholarly interpretation from publications.

## Research scope

Region: Jauntal/Podjuna, Carinthia, Austria, including Globasnitz/Iuenna, Hemmaberg, Jaunstein, Sankt Stefan, and the wider Drau/Drava landscape.

Principal archaeological contexts include Roman Noricum, Late Antiquity, and the Early Middle Ages, alongside wider regional archaeological and historiographic materials.

Data types include excavation documentation, databases, GIS/geodata, geophysical surveys, photographs, drawings, plans, texts, tables, environmental archaeological data, architectural documentation, 3D data, and retrodigitized archival records.

Top-level archival groups include Hemmaberg (HB), Globasnitz (GLO), Jaunstein (JAU), Sankt Stefan (STE), Jauntal (TAL), and Retrodigitalisate (RET).

## Project context

IUENNA was funded through the Go!Digital 3.0 programme of the Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW). Project partners and contributing institutions include kärnten.museum, the Austrian Archaeological Institute (ÖAI/ÖAW), ACDH-CH/ÖAW, the Austrian Federal Monuments Authority (BDA), and ARDIG – Archäologischer Dienst GesmbH.

The project follows FAIR-oriented research-data-management principles and uses ARCHE for sustainable long-term preservation.

## Data freshness

The IUENNA web layer is generated from the archived corpus. For changing repository metadata, rights, access status, or version-specific questions, treat the corresponding ARCHE record as authoritative.

Canonical AI discovery entry point: https://iuenna.github.io/llms.txt
